facts: Insured was hospitalized for suspected malaria, but pathological tests showed no blood parasites and there was no medical advice for hospitalization. The insurer's repudiation was upheld.
Claim for backache was repudiated, and the insured made a representation after 18 months, rendering the complaint time-barred under policy conditions. Complaint dismissed.
Wife underwent ear surgery and claim was rejected for pre-existing chronic mastoiditis. The medical opinion was speculative rather than definitive, so the insurer was ordered to pay.
Personal Accident claim where insurer initially offered 3 weeks temporary total disablement, later revised to 5 weeks. Surgeon recommended 6 weeks, which was awarded.
Personal accident claim experienced delay in paying temporary total disablement. The complainant already received the balance amount and sought better administrative efficiency. Case closed.
Claim for laminectomy was repudiated for delayed filing and pre-existing spinal stenosis. Proof established the policy was active since 1999, waiving time limits. Claim allowed with deductions.
Wife underwent TKR after policy running for 14 years. Insured repudiated based on old X-ray reports showing osteoarthritis. Repudiation set aside and full relief granted.
Husband underwent rectopexy and hernia repair. Claim repudiated due to pre-existing condition, supported by statements signed by the insured regarding long-term symptoms. Dismissed.
Child underwent appendectomy, but claim was rejected citing 2-year prior stomach pain. Explanation found convincing and doctor's certificate gave weight, so repudiation was set aside.
Insurer reduced cumulative bonus citing a 9-day renewal delay, offering a lower payout. Ombudsman noted consistent policy treatment and awarded full claim with cumulative bonus.
Claim for hysterectomy was repudiated under exclusion. During hearing, the insurer could not trace the file or justify the cut, and agreed to pay the full claimed amount.

Daughter was operated for correction of congenital absence of vagina. Insurer rejected under external congenital anomaly exclusion. Ombudsman ruled it a congenital deformity, setting aside the rejection.
Claim for fracture treatment was rejected claiming hospitalization was unnecessary and under 24 hours. Ombudsman noted treatment was under specialist advice and time of discharge was missing.
Claim for piles and colitis rejected because the hospital had only 8 beds and unqualified nurses, despite the medical report admitting validity. Ombudsman ordered payment.
Accidental ankle injury claim rejected because the complainant had pre-existing diabetes linked to wound healing. Ombudsman ruled exclusions should not defeat the main purpose of the cover.
First-year hysterectomy claim rejected due to pre-existing irregular periods mentioned in hospital notes. Ombudsman found no evidence of pre-existing cancer and set aside repudiation.
Claim for kidney failure was repudiated based on pre-existing chronic renal failure and diabetes history. Conflicting medical opinions led to upholding the repudiation.
Claim rejected on grounds of pre-existing palpitation. Insurer failed to provide cogent evidence or consultation papers proving the exact duration prior to policy inception. Allowed.
Incisional hernia surgery claim repudiated because hernia developed on the scar of an undisclosed prior appendicectomy. Repudiation upheld for non-disclosure.
Two-year-old child operated for cataract, claim rejected as congenital. One medical referee found the claim admissible without confirming it as congenital, so order was passed to pay.

Complainant's son was hospitalised for epilepsy. Insurer repudiated claim citing non-disclosure of pre-existing epilepsy and treating the policy as new due to a break in continuity from previous group policy. Ombudsman upheld repudiation.

Insurer refused to renew complainant's wife's mediclaim policy. Ombudsman held that renewal cannot be refused simply due to claims or onerous risk resulting from contracted diseases during the policy period, directing the insurer to renew the policy.

Complainant met with an accident and was hospitalised after initial treatment. Insurer repudiated claim arguing it could have been treated conservatively without admission. Ombudsman set aside repudiation as hospitalisation was on doctor's advice.

Complainant's mother was hospitalised and claim was rejected under exclusion clauses relating to pre-existing diabetes and pre-hospitalisation consultations. Ombudsman noted diabetes was declared at inception without exclusion, setting aside repudiation.

Complainant underwent CABG. Claim was repudiated for suppression of pre-existing ischemic heart disease and diabetes, which was established by hospital records prior to policy inception. Complaint dismissed.

Complainant's wife underwent surgery for incisional hernia which developed on the scar of an earlier hysterectomy. Insurer invoked exclusion clauses linking the current condition to the past surgery. Repudiation sustained.

Complainant's wife underwent surgery for tubo-ovarian mass. Insurer rejected claim because the hospital had fewer than 15 in-patient beds as per exclusion rules. Ombudsman ruled the marginal short-fall in beds was not fundamental enough to deny benefits.

Complainant's wife underwent knee replacement surgery. Insurer offered a reduced settlement based on historical tabular benefit limits, linking it to an osteotomy performed eight years prior. Ombudsman held the reduction unjustified and awarded the full amount.

Complainant underwent surgery for fistula in anus. Claim was repudiated under waiting period exclusion clauses as there was a 73-day gap in policy renewal, making it a fresh policy and the surgery occurred within the first year.

Complainant's wife suffered accidental fracture and was hospitalised. Insurer offered a reduced amount due to duplicate bills and excluded payments. During hearing, insurer conceded payments against duplicate bills backed by affidavit were admissible. Full claim awarded with interest.

Complainant's daughter was hospitalised and underwent surgery. Insurer initially repudiated on pre-existence grounds, then sent a reduced discharge voucher, but ultimately admitted during the hearing that repudiation was wrong and full amount was payable. Awarded with interest.

Complainant sought reimbursement for hospitalisation and surgery. Insurer disallowed a portion because the medical bill voucher was issued on the hospital's letterhead. Ombudsman directed full payment with interest.

Complainant underwent PTCA for unstable angina. Insurer repudiated claim alleging suppression of past cardiac history and non-submission of documents. Ombudsman noted insurer's panel doctor had medically examined and certified the complainant fit prior to policy issuance, setting aside repudiation.

Insurer issued a 15-day notice of cancellation for a running mediclaim policy without providing specific reasons. Ombudsman held the cancellation bad in law due to inadequate notice period and lack of valid reasons, setting it aside.

Complainant's son underwent laminectomy for backache in the first year of the policy. Insurer repudiated on pre-existence grounds. Ombudsman noted medical referee opinions were inconclusive or favored the insured, thus setting aside repudiation.

Complainant's wife underwent CABG. Insurer repudiated for non-disclosure of past insurance in proposal form. Ombudsman observed that the insurer had treated the policy as continuous by awarding cumulative bonuses, effectively knowing of past coverage, and thus estopped from denying liability.

Complainant's wife was hospitalised after weeks of OPD treatment. Insurer repudiated the claim based on a medical referee's opinion that it could be treated as OPD. Ombudsman set aside repudiation given the treating doctor's prolonged care and prolonged policy standing.

Complainant was hospitalised for tuberculosis. Claim was repudiated under pre-existing disease clause based on a panel doctor's presumptive opinion. Ombudsman found no evidence of pre-existence prior to policy inception and ordered full payment.

Complainant underwent left eye cataract surgery but failed to disclose a prior right eye cataract operation in the proposal form. Suppression of material fact was established, and repudiation was upheld.

Under a personal accident policy, the complainant sustained injuries in a scooter accident. Insurer offered 3 weeks temporary total disablement against 6 weeks advised by the treating doctor. Ombudsman applied the golden mean principle and awarded 4.5 weeks compensation.

Wife of the complainant underwent TKR. Claim repudiated for delayed submission, non-disclosure of past Hysterectomy, and Cervical Spondylosis. Ombudsman noted that treated and cured Spondylosis from 4 years prior cannot be a sole reason to repudiate TKR and non-disclosure was not proved material. Repudiation set aside.

Complainant was hospitalised and claim was repudiated as treatment could be on OPD basis. Treating doctor certified hospitalisation was necessary. Repudiation set aside in the first case. In the second companion case involving the same insurer, hospitalisation ended in angiography and diagnosis only, so repudiation was upheld under policy clause 4.10.

Wife of the complainant was hospitalised. Claim repudiated on the ground that hospitalisation was not necessary and treatment could be done in OPD. Ombudsman observed hospitalisation was on the advice of a qualified surgeon. Repudiation set aside.

Complainant's wife diagnosed with ruptured ectopic pregnancy. Claim repudiated under exclusion clause 4.12 for conditions traceable to pregnancy, which was upheld. In a companion case against National Insurance, a claim for Ovarian Cyst and Appendicitis was repudiated for pre-existence based on a written statement by the insured; repudiation sustained.

Insurer deducted a portion of hospitalisation expenses based on medical referee opinion. Subsequently, the same medical referee issued an opinion advising release of the deducted amount. No justification for withholding found. Insurer directed to pay the balance.

Daughter of complainant hospitalised for ENT problem. Claim repudiated as domiciliary treatment was sufficient and the hospital did not meet policy condition 2.1 regarding registration/bed strength. Ombudsman held infrastructural shortfall is not tenable for repudiation. Insurer directed to pay.

Claim for hospitalisation and treatment of Gouty Synovitis repudiated under clause 4.1 and medical referee opinion that hospitalisation was unnecessary. Policy was in force for 15 years. Hospitalisation was under advice of treating surgeon. Repudiation set aside.

In the first case, parties reached an amicable settlement of Rs. 4856 for a Tonsillectomy claim. In the second case against New India Assurance regarding back-ache hospitalisation, claim was repudiated for lack of active treatment and rest only; ombudsman ruled in favour of complainant as hospitalisation was under medical advice and policy was long-standing.

Complainant underwent bilateral knee replacements. Insurer settled left knee claim but repudiated right knee claim citing pre-existence and 4th-year policy restrictions. Ombudsman found no blanket policy exclusions for 4th-year claims or proof of pre-existing osteoarthritis. Insurer directed to pay.

Wife of complainant underwent vaginal hysterectomy. Claim repudiated on grounds of undisclosed prior miscarriages and D&E. Ombudsman noted no proof that miscarriages occurred prior to policy inception in 1999, and medical referee's post-script advising rejection lacked weight. Repudiation set aside.

In the first case against Oriental Insurance, the insurer failed to appear or defend the file, and was ordered to pay the claim. In the second case against New India Assurance, claim for Aortic Stenosis and Rheumatic Heart Disease was repudiated on pre-existing grounds due to age. Ombudsman ruled generic blanket exclusions for RHD are unfair. Insurer to pay full amount with interest.

Claim for hospitalisation of complainant's mother repudiated under exclusion clause 4.1. Discharge summary showed history of CVA for the past 2 years, which was accepted as admissible evidence. Repudiation upheld.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Under a floater policy, complainant claimed for bilateral cataract surgeries. Insurer paid for the right eye but treated the left eye as 'no claim' because the maximum limit for cataract had been exhausted. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision based on policy limits. In a companion case against National Insurance regarding Cortical Sinus Thrombosis, repudiation on pre-existing grounds was set aside and Rs. 1,07,474 awarded.

Insurer refused renewal of mediclaim policy without medical tests, alleging delay, despite receiving the renewal cheque before the due date. Ombudsman found no delay and directed the insurer to renew the policy continuously without break upon collecting the premium.

Complainant operated for CAD twice within 45 days. Insurer repudiated claims citing varying durations of diabetes (19 years vs 7-8 years) in hospital summaries and short interval between surgeries. Ombudsman gave benefit of doubt to complainant as evidence was contradictory. Insurer to pay Rs. 2,61,000.

Complainant's son sustained severe injuries in an explosion and was admitted for observation. Claim repudiated on the ground that admission was for observation only. Ombudsman noted the insurer's action was too rigid given the emergency circumstances of an injured child. Insurer to pay Rs. 2,629.

Claim for gynaecological problem (Dysfunctional Uterine Bleeding) repudiated alleging pre-existence 15-20 years back. Medical records and treating gynecologist certified the condition was acute and of 8 months duration. Benefit of doubt given to complainant due to conflicting documents. Insurer to pay Rs. 45,971.

Complainant experienced severe delay in claim settlement through the TPA. Insurer sent a discharge voucher for a slightly lesser amount after grievance intervention but could not justify the deduction. Claim allowed for full amount along with 8% simple interest.

Claim for CABG surgery repudiated after insurer issued policy documents with cardiac disorders excluded following a 5-month renewal break. Computer-generated policy initially showed no exclusions, and exclusion documents were only sent after claim lodging. Repudiation set aside. Insurer to pay Rs. 1,60,582.

Complainant disputed the imposition of exclusions and lack of cumulative bonus after switching from a group policy to an individual policy with New India Assurance. Insurer passed an endorsement removing exclusions for the first year and issuing the second year without exclusions. Complainant expressed satisfaction; complaint disposed.

Insured claimed for fracture treatment. Insurer repudiated based on hospital eligibility criteria, but hospital was registered and networked with TPAs. Ombudsman ordered payment of Rs. 5370 with 8 percent interest.

Two similar cases where claims were initially repudiated for exclusions or pre-existing conditions, but insurers later reconsidered, issued discharge vouchers for Rs. 7000 and Rs. 28000 respectively, and payments were accepted by complainants, closing the complaints.

Complainant hospitalized for tonsils. Claim repudiated alleging pre-existing condition since last 3 years based on doctor report, but report lacked such mention and insurer failed to produce proposal or underwriting records. Insurer ordered to pay Rs. 20837.
Insured underwent IVF after unsuccessful laparoscopic surgery for infertility. Claim repudiated under policy clause excluding sterility. Ombudsman upheld repudiation.

Claim for osteoporosis and other conditions repudiated as pre-existing based on an old proposal form from 1999, despite continuous renewals and new ailments developing later. Repudiation set aside and claim ordered to be settled.

Bypass surgery claim repudiated alleging suppression of pre-existing angina and a mild stroke in 1995-1996. Ombudsman awarded Rs. 111031 as discharge certificate did not specify exact duration and insurer lacked employer records or doctor statements.
Claim for exorbitant medical expenses following hemicolectomy delayed on pretext of investigation. Ombudsman directed insurer to pay sum insured of Rs. 320000.

Angioplasty claim repudiated on ground of pre-existing hypertension, despite long policy history. Cardiologist opinion showed no definitive prior record. Ombudsman awarded Rs. 210000 including claim-free bonus.
Overseas mediclaim for hydrocephalus surgery rejected due to non-disclosure of past brain surgery and high blood pressure, and because treatment was for a non-emergent condition. Complaint dismissed.

Claim for frozen shoulder treatment at an ayurvedic centre repudiated on grounds that hospitalization was unnecessary. Ombudsman held that hospitalization necessity is decided by the treating physician, not the insurer, and ordered payment.

Claim for neurological observation after a fall repudiated as hospitalization was allegedly for investigation only. Ombudsman held admission was on specialist advice and tests were part of treatment, ordering payment.
Insurer disallowed admission fee and room service charges. Ombudsman found nursing service charges and admission fees are valid reimbursable expenses, awarding Rs. 190.

Granddaughter's post aural abscess claim repudiated as pre-existing because of an ear swelling 5-6 years prior. Ombudsman held that full recovery means recurrence is not a pre-existing disease and ordered payment.
CABG claim repudiated due to pre-existing long-standing diabetes and hypertension. Complainant submitted tampered medical certificates to mislead the forum. Complaint dismissed.

Varicose veins claim repudiated and policy cancelled alleging 12-year pre-existing ailment and non-disclosure. Investigation confirmed disease duration was only 1.5 years. Insurer ordered to reimburse expenses and restore policy.
Chronic liver disease claim repudiated based on a test report mistakenly dated prior to policy inception instead of the actual later date. Insurer directed to reimburse medical expenses.
Claim for hypertension and giddiness repudiated as hospitalization was solely for investigation without significant hospital treatment, with diagnostic scans done outside. Complaint dismissed.

COPD claim repudiated as pre-existing. Insurer admitted policy inception predated the illness onset and agreed to settle, but TPA delayed. Ombudsman ordered settlement up to sum insured of Rs. 60000 plus 8 percent interest.
Hemiplegia claim repudiated due to non-disclosure of 15-year diabetes history which had a medically acknowledged nexus to the stroke. Complaint dismissed.
Angioplasty claim repudiated under exclusion clause as CAD pre-existed the policy inception, supported by past hospital records from 1996. Complaint dismissed.

Insured underwent repair of split ear lobule and depressed scar. Insurer repudiated the claim stating treatment was cosmetic and excluded under the policy. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation as no accidental happening was proved.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured was hospitalised for Chronic Sinusitis/Deviated Nasal Septum and underwent FESS/Septoplasty. Insurer repudiated claim citing 15 years history of nose block. Attending doctor later certified history as 1 year. Ombudsman held pre-existence not tenable and directed payment.

Insured claimed reimbursement for treatment of fissure in ano, BPH, hemorrhoids, DM, HTN, and gastric ulcer. Insurer repudiated entire claim citing pre-existing HTN, excluded DM, and waiting period for piles. Ombudsman held treatment for fissure in ano and gastric ulcer were independent and directed reimbursement for those.

Insured underwent CABG for CAD. Claim was partially settled because chest pain manifested one month before sum insured was increased from Rs. 1,00,000 to Rs. 2,00,000. Ombudsman upheld the settlement restricted to pre-increased sum insured.

Insured's wife was hospitalised for Bilateral Ovarian Cyst and underwent laparoscopy. Insurer repudiated claim stating hospitalisation was related to infertility treatment. Medical opinion confirmed surgery was primarily for ovarian cyst, making infertility procedure incidental. Repudiation set aside.

Insured was hospitalised for multiple renal calculi 10 months after policy inception. Insurer repudiated claim as pre-existing. Ombudsman noted lack of evidence of prior symptoms and attending doctor's opinion that stones could form in 5-6 months, setting aside repudiation.

Insured claimed for hemoptysis, aortic stenosis, and coronary artery disease. Insurer repudiated claim citing pre-existing pulmonary tuberculosis causing hemoptysis. Ombudsman held hemoptysis was linked to prior TB but aortic stenosis and CAD were unrelated, directing payment for unrelated treatments.

Insured's spouse was hospitalised for Cervical Cerclage due to cervical incompetence. Insurer repudiated claim under exclusion for treatments related to pregnancy or childbirth. Ombudsman upheld repudiation as procedure was for maintenance of pregnancy.

Insured underwent PTCA for Ischaemic Heart Disease. Claim was repudiated because insured had a 15-20 year history of hypertension, a risk factor for CAD. Ombudsman upheld repudiation establishing hypertension as pre-existing proximate cause.

Insured was hospitalised for portal hypertension, hepatic failure, and alcoholic liver disease. Insurer repudiated claim under exclusion for diseases arising from alcohol consumption. Ombudsman upheld insurer's decision based on medical records confirming alcoholic cirrhosis.

Insured was hospitalized for ureteric calculus under Universal Health Insurance Policy. Insurer repudiated claim for pre-existence and hospital bed capacity violation. Ombudsman noted bed condition was not communicated to insured and allowed 75% on ex-gratia basis.

Insured claimed for injuries sustained in a road accident while traveling as a pillion rider. Insurer rejected claim under exclusion for alcohol use. Ombudsman held insurer failed to prove intoxication caused the accident and ordered claim payment.

Insured's 7-year-old daughter was hospitalised for Chronic Adeno Tonsilitis. Insurer repudiated claim as pre-existing. Ombudsman noted medical records traced symptoms only to a date after policy inception and set aside repudiation.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured's wife underwent CABG for CAD. Insurer repudiated claim under pre-existing disease exclusion citing history of hypertension since 1980 and TIA. Ombudsman upheld repudiation establishing hypertension as proximate cause for CAD.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Insured underwent CABG for Coronary Artery Disease. Insurer repudiated claim citing old myocardial infarction 20 years ago. Ombudsman noted insured remained asymptomatic and unmedicated for 20 years, making pre-existence untenable, and ordered claim payment.

Overseas medical policy claim for US$ 1147.59 was partly settled by foreign settling agent. Insurer failed to provide balance due to internal communication issues with agent. Ombudsman directed insurer to settle the balance amount immediately.

Overseas mediclaim policy claim was repudiated for pre-existing chest pain. Ombudsman noted policy defines pre-existing conditions as treatments sought within 12 months prior to travel, and no such treatment occurred, but dismissed the specific petition text outcome formulation due to mislabeling in source text summary logic.
Insurer refused to renew mediclaim policy due to bad claim experience after continuous renewals from 1992 to 2004. Ombudsman held refusal was arbitrary and directed renewal upon payment of premium.
Insurer disallowed Rs. 7,000 for a ceramic crown fixed to teeth injured in a road accident, citing cosmetic exclusion. Ombudsman held crown was necessitated by accident and ordered payment.

Insured's mother underwent operation for hidradenitis under general anesthesia. Insurer repudiated claim for hospitalization under 24 hours. Ombudsman held operation required proper operation theater and ordered claim allowance.

Claim was repudiated because the insured was admitted for investigation only, which did not require hospitalisation and could have been done on an OPD basis. Separately, a small balance for pre-natal expenses was discussed in another claim part.

The insured underwent bypass surgery for blockages detected shortly after policy inception. Medical records from a prior hospital confirmed a known history of hypertension, diabetes, and ischemic heart disease which was not declared in the proposal form.
Claim for an operation of an abscess behind the knee was repudiated because hospital confinement was less than 24 hours, violating the minimum 24-hour hospitalization policy condition.

The insured underwent a hysterectomy due to a ruptured ectopic pregnancy and cornual pregnancy complications. The insurer repudiated the claim on the ground that pregnancy is an excluded condition under the standard mediclaim policy.

Complainant underwent surgery for gall bladder stones shortly after policy inception. The insurer repudiated the claim based on panel doctor opinion that chronic cholecystitis existed for 1 to 2 years prior to policy inception.

Claim was repudiated after 1.5 years on the ground that the patient was admitted only for investigations and tests rather than actual treatment, and the records showed no specific treatment for porphyria.

The insurer imposed a high compulsory excess of Rs. 5000 per claim on a Rs. 20000 sum insured due to a high claim ratio on a long-standing policy. The Ombudsman held the 25 percent excess unreasonable for senior citizens and advised replacing it with a small token excess for small claims.

Complainant underwent emergency laparotomy for an ovarian cyst and ruptured appendix shortly after policy inception. The insurer repudiated the claim as pre-existing based on previous medical history of ovarian cystectomy and prior symptoms.

Claim for rheumatic heart disease treatment was repudiated on grounds of pre-existing disease, supported by medical consensus that valve involvement takes years to develop. Additionally, a dental claim was rejected due to lack of hospitalization.

TPA deducted a small amount for home visits from a hospitalisation claim without proper review of policy terms. The Ombudsman held that deductions without giving the insured an opportunity to represent were improper and directed re-examination.

The claim for an ovarian tumor and urinary dilatation treatment was delayed indefinitely by the TPA despite all details being submitted. The Ombudsman criticized the reckless irresponsibility of the TPA and ordered settlement.
Hysterectomy expenses were rejected because there was a break in insurance due to non-renewal during the grace period, making the policy a fresh contract and hitting first-year exclusion clauses.

Claim for angioplasty was repudiated alleging 30 years of hypertension was undisclosed in the proposal. The Ombudsman found the entry was likely a clerical error for 30 days given the insured's foreign manual labor with routine medical checks, and allowed the claim up to sum insured.

Claim for liver cirrhosis and hypertension was repudiated for non-disclosure of prior diabetes and liver condition. While upholding the repudiation due to admitted prior illness, the Ombudsman awarded an ex-gratia amount considering the claimant's poor health and financial distress.

Hernia surgery claim was repudiated and policy cancelled due to undisclosed history of prior hernia repair. Although cancellation without proper notice was faulted, the repudiation and cancellation of the policy were upheld.
Accident claim for a bathroom fall was rejected because records showed treatment was actually for an ayurvedic rheumatic condition rather than a visible accidental injury.

Surgical treatment for deflected nasal septum in the complainant's daughter was rejected as a congenital disorder. The Ombudsman held that deflected nasal septum without external deformity does not constitute a congenital external exclusion and ordered payment.

Claim for oral carcinoma treatment was delayed and contested based on a disputed investigator statement regarding disease duration. Finding no proof of pre-existing disease or misrepresentation, the Ombudsman allowed the claim.
Claim reimbursement for wife's treatment was rejected because the condition was attributable to pregnancy, which is explicitly excluded under policy clause 4.12.

Claim for osteosarcoma and leg amputation of the insured's son was repudiated for alleged suppression of prior illness dates. The Ombudsman found the date discrepancy was an inadvertent clerical error and no suppression existed, ordering full claim payment.
Insured claimed reimbursement for hospitalisation due to Seborrhic Dermatitis. Insurer rejected the claim citing pre-existing Diabetes mellitus of 5 years not disclosed in the proposal form.
Claim for son's treatment of kidney problems and Urinary Tract Infection was repudiated due to pre-existing nature of the disease and misrepresentation.
Claim for father's treatment was rejected because he suffered from pre-existing Diabetes Mellitus which was concealed at the time of taking the policy.

Insurer rejected mediclaim on the grounds that admission was for general checkup and investigation, and patient was under medication for 5 years. Ombudsman found medication claim unproven and ordered payment for actual medicine bills.
Insurer closed mediclaim because the insured obtained the policy after knowing about her disease, concealing material facts at the time of proposal.

Claim for cancer treatment was repudiated alleging pre-existing symptoms from policy inception. Ombudsman noted panel doctor's report was insufficient to prove prior knowledge and set aside the rejection.
Claim for piles surgery was partially paid based on the original sum insured of Rs. 50,000 rather than the enhanced Rs. 2,00,000, as the condition pre-dated the enhancement waiting period.
Insurer rejected claim for a fracture treated with plaster on the grounds that hospitalisation was not required. Ombudsman ruled that restricted movement for 5 weeks qualified for reimbursement.
Claim for Disc Derangement syndrome was rejected citing pre-existing lower back pain. Ombudsman noted renewal without fresh proposal made the rejection untenable and ordered full payment.
Insurer partially paid dental treatment claim based on expert opinion. Ombudsman found no reason to disbelieve the complainant and ordered full reimbursement.
Claim for medical expenses was rejected for suppression of material facts regarding mother's pre-existing Hypertension and Periarthritis at proposal and revival.

Claim for Hernia was rejected alleging pre-existing symptoms for 5 years. Ombudsman set aside the repudiation noting the insured was a bank employee eligible for full medical refund anyway, indicating lack of prior awareness.

Insurer partially paid claim, denying expenses beyond 30 days of pre-hospitalisation and 60 days post-hospitalisation, and rejected a hand-written professional fee bill due to late submission and questionable credibility.
Claim for wife's treatment of Rheumatoid Arthritis was repudiated for pre-existing nature of the disease and non-disclosure of vital information.

insurer: The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
facts: Claim for Incisional Hernia Post Hysterectomy was rejected because the treatment was a continuation of a pre-existing condition spanning 4 years prior to the policy.
Ear surgery claim was rejected as hospital records showed symptoms existed within the first 30 days of the policy period, attracting the waiting period exclusion.

Insurer rejected child's claim for Acute Glomerulo Nephritis and Acute Gastro Enteritis assuming it was a longstanding problem. Ombudsman allowed the claim as the insurer failed to establish prior illness.
Claim for Acute Angle Closure Glaucoma was rejected alleging pre-existing condition. Hospital records proved sudden onset within 1-3 days, so the Ombudsman allowed the claim.
Claim for diabetic foot treatment was rejected because hospital records proved the insured had diabetes for 23 years, constituting suppression of material facts.
Claim for heart treatment was rejected because renewal payment cheque bounced, causing a break in policy continuity; the new policy commenced later, and the illness predated it.

Complainant sought reimbursement for wife's incisional hernia surgery. Insurer rejected claim citing pre-existing condition, as the hernia developed at the site of a previous caesarean section performed six years prior to policy commencement. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Policyholder underwent treatment for cardiac diseases and died of heart disease. Insurer rejected the claim for non-disclosure of pre-existing heart ailments from 1995 when renewing the policy after a gap. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint due to intentional suppression of material facts.

Claim for inguinal hernia treatment was rejected due to non-disclosure of pre-existing medical history dating back years before policy inception. Ombudsman upheld dismissal based on suppression of material facts.

Claim for low back ache hospitalisation was repudiated due to a duration discrepancy between the discharge summary and medical certificate. The doctor later rectified the summary. Ombudsman allowed the claim, ruling the initial discrepancy was a minor clerical error by a non-attending junior doctor.

Claim for father's treatment of portal hypertension and cirrhosis under a group mediclaim policy was repudiated due to pre-existing disease of 8 years. Considering the complainant's severe financial distress, the Ombudsman awarded an ex-gratia amount while upholding the repudiation.

Insurer rejected a renal transplantation claim citing pre-existing illness based on a bland hospital record statement. Ombudsman found no substantive medical evidence of prior kidney ailments, ruled the insurer's decision invalid, and ordered settlement of the claim.

Claim for treatment received at a hospital in Kenya and subsequent outpatient treatment in Trivandrum was rejected because the policy permitted reimbursement only for inpatient hospital treatment in India. Ombudsman upheld the repudiation.
Claim for thyroid gland surgery was repudiated as pre-existing. Investigations and large surgical dimensions proved the ailment existed for several years. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

Claim for treatment at a nursing home was rejected because the facility did not conform to the policy's definition of a hospital registered with local authorities. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's decision.

Claim for an abortion operation due to severe bleeding was rejected under policy clause 4.12 excluding pregnancy-related complications. Records did not prove it was a life-saving procedure. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

Claim for hospitalisation under a Jana Seva Insurance Policy was rejected due to alleged pre-existing disease. At the Ombudsman's intervention, parties compromised, and the insurer agreed to pay an amount in full and final settlement.
Complainant sought compensation for a 100-day delay by the TPA in settling a mediclaim. Ombudsman allowed travelling expenses and short-term interest on the settled claim amount.
Claim for coronary artery bypass surgery was rejected because the insured suffered from the illness prior to proposing for insurance and failed to disclose it. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

Claim for abdominal hysterectomy was rejected as the operation occurred during the policy exclusion period. During the hearing, the complainant expressed willingness to withdraw the case, leading to dismissal.

Claim for hernia surgery was rejected on the grounds that it was an after-effect of a hysterectomy performed 7 years prior to the policy and not disclosed in the proposal. Ombudsman upheld the rejection but awarded an ex-gratia amount due to the complainant's financial hardship.

Claim for oesophagitis and sinusitis hospitalisation was rejected on the basis that hospitalisation was unnecessary. The Ombudsman found issues with policy validity due to bigamy, but awarded hospital charges as ex-gratia considering the complainant's impecunious condition.

Claim for high myopia astigmatism surgery was rejected because the condition was pre-existing from childhood, as confirmed by family testimony regarding spectacles use. Ombudsman dismissed the complaint.

Insurer partially rejected a bypass surgery claim citing pre-existing diabetes and TURP history not disclosed in the proposal. Ombudsman found the insurer's reasoning arbitrary and directed payment of the sum insured under a secondary policy.

Complainant sought full reimbursement for post-hospitalisation expenses following heart attacks. Insurer disallowed expenses incurred beyond the 60-day policy limit. Ombudsman upheld the insurer's strict adherence to policy conditions and dismissed the complaint.

Insurer rejected claims for Motor Neuron Disease citing pre-existing neck pain and spondylosis. Ombudsman ruled that initial neck pain treatments were pre-existing and properly rejected, but the subsequent Motor Neuron Disease developed during policy coverage and ordered payment for those specific treatments.
